engines.name: 3.5L twin-turbo V6 with electric supercharger (48V mild hybrid)

issues.t: Turbo oil feed pipe can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Burning-oil smell, light smoke from under the hood, or oil spots under the car. Some owners first notice an oil warning light.
issues.why: The oil feed pipe to the left turbocharger can wear out or lose its seal and drip oil onto the hot exhaust. Genesis first recalled the pipe in 2019, then widened the recall in 2024 with a new part, so cars fixed the first time need the newer repair too.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the Genesis or NHTSA recall lookup. If you smell burning oil or see smoke, stop driving and have the car towed to a dealer. The pipe is replaced free.

issues.t: Starter solenoid can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. In some cases a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, even with the car parked.
issues.why: Water can get into the starter solenoid and cause a short circuit, which can start an engine-bay fire whether the car is running or not. Owners were told to park outside until the fix is done. Some owners report waiting for parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls. Until the repair is done, park outside and away from buildings. The dealer installs a relay kit for free.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may hesitate, lose power or stall while driving, and it may not restart.
issues.why: The fuel pump in certain 2022 and 2023 Genesis cars can fail, which starves the engine of fuel. This recall widened an earlier one that covered fewer cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer will inspect the pump and replace it for free. If the car stalls, get safely off the road and have it towed.

issues.t: Fuel can leak at the fuel rail connection (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell around the car or from the engine bay, sometimes inside the cabin.
issues.why: The joint where the fuel pipe meets the fuel rail on the engine may not seal fully, so fuel can seep out near hot parts and raise the risk of fire.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't keep driving it. Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer tightens or replaces the fuel pipe for free.

issues.t: Sudden braking from Highway Drive Assist radar (recall)
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on the highway for no reason while Highway Drive Assist is on, sometimes with nothing ahead.
issues.why: A corner radar used by Highway Drive Assist can falsely sense another vehicle, which makes the system brake suddenly. Genesis advised owners not to use the feature until the repair is done.
issues.next: Don't use Highway Drive Assist until the recall is done. The dealer replaces the front bumper beam free of charge.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The digital gauge cluster goes dark or freezes, so you may not see your speed or warning lights.
issues.why: A software error can make the instrument panel display fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for the recall. The fix is a free software update, done over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: Front seat belt anchors can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Often no sign at all. You might notice a seat belt anchor that moves or rattles near the floor beside the seat.
issues.why: The anchors that hold the driver and front passenger seat belts may not be fixed firmly enough and can detach in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer will inspect the anchors and reinforce or replace them for free.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioners can throw metal fragments (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving. The danger only shows up when the belts fire in a crash.
issues.why: On certain 2023 cars, the front and rear seat belt pretensioners can rupture when they deploy, sending metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the dealer replace the parts for free.

issues.t: Windshield or rear glass may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: You may hear wind noise or a creak around the glass, or see the glass shift in its frame.
issues.why: The wrong primer may have been used when the windshield and rear window were installed, so the glue may not hold. The glass could come loose while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer replaces the front and rear glass for free.

issues.t: Oil leaks from turbo lines or engine seals
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell, smoke from under the hood, or low-oil warnings between changes.
issues.why: Besides the recalled left-side pipe, owners report leaks from the right-side turbo oil line, turbo seals and O-rings on the 3.3L engine. One owner was refused goodwill because the recall covered only the left side.
issues.next: Have the leak traced right away, because oil dripping on the exhaust is a fire risk. Ask the dealer whether a service bulletin or the recall applies before paying.

issues.t: Repeated overheating and thermostat failures
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, the engine warning light comes on, or the car overheats, sometimes again after a repair.
issues.why: Several owners of 2017 cars report the thermostat and water pump being replaced more than once and the overheating coming back.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if the gauge is high, since driving hot can ruin the engine. Keep records of each repair and ask for a full cooling system diagnosis.

issues.t: Shifter won't engage gear or drops into neutral
issues.sym: The car doesn't go into Drive or Reverse on the first try, slips into Neutral when the shifter is bumped, or is slow to respond when pulling away.
issues.why: Owners of early cars report the electronic gear selector and 8-speed automatic not responding as expected, with harsh or delayed shifts at low speed.
issues.next: Always check the gear display before you let go of the brake. Have the dealer check for software updates and stored codes.

issues.t: Hesitation when pulling away from a stop
issues.sym: You press the gas from a stop and nothing happens for a second or two, then the car surges. It is worst when turning into traffic.
issues.why: Several owners report this delay and dealers often find no fault code. It appears tied to throttle and transmission programming rather than a broken part.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for engine and transmission software updates and to road-test it with you. Leave extra room when pulling out until it is fixed.

issues.t: Car goes completely dead or won't start
issues.sym: The car shuts down or won't power up at all, sometimes in traffic. Screens and lights may go dark.
issues.why: Owners report sudden electrical failures. In one case the dealer found water-corroded wiring. A weak 12-volt battery can cause similar trouble.
issues.next: Have the battery, charging system and main wiring checked, and look for water getting in. Also make sure the starter recall is done.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on the intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, a slight loss of power or a misfire code at higher mileage.
issues.why: These direct-injection engines spray fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes the backs of the intake valves. Oil vapor from the crankcase vent bakes onto them over time.
issues.next: Use good fuel and change the oil on time. If you have a rough idle or misfire codes, ask about a walnut-blasting valve cleaning.

issues.t: Tires wear out early, blow out or vibrate
issues.sym: Bald or damaged tires much sooner than expected, a sidewall blowout, or a steady vibration at speed.
issues.why: Owners of these heavy sedans report fast wear and several tire failures, and a vibration traced to the factory tires. The tire maker and Genesis sometimes disagree on who covers it.
issues.next: Check tire pressure and tread often, and get an alignment if wear is uneven. Ask the tire maker about its warranty if they fail early.

issues.t: Self-leveling headlights aim too high or too low
issues.sym: The headlights point at the road right in front of you or into the eyes of other drivers, and the aim doesn't correct itself.
issues.why: The automatic headlight leveling system can lose its calibration or fail to adjust.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the leveling sensor and recalibrate the headlights.

issues.t: Steering sticks or lane assist pulls too hard
issues.sym: The steering wheel doesn't return to center after a turn, or the lane-keeping system tugs the wheel sharply.
issues.why: Owners report sticking electric steering and lane assist steering the car harder than expected.
issues.next: Have the steering system and its sensors checked. Turn lane-keeping off if it pulls unexpectedly until the dealer looks at it.

issues.t: False crash warnings and sudden automatic stops
issues.sym: Collision warnings go off with nothing in front, and the car may brake on its own.
issues.why: The forward collision sensors can give false alerts. One owner reports repeat dealer repairs that did not cure it.
issues.next: Keep the front sensor area clean. Have the dealer check sensor aim and software, and document every event.

issues.t: Rodents chew through engine wiring
issues.sym: Warning lights, airbag light on, or a no-start after the car sits outside. You may find nests or chewed wires under the hood.
issues.why: Mice and rats can chew wiring harnesses in the engine bay. One owner reported a major airbag wiring repair.
issues.next: Check your comprehensive insurance, which often covers rodent damage. Use rodent tape or deterrents if you park outdoors.

issues.t: Leather seats fade or wear early
issues.sym: The seat leather looks faded or worn on the front and rear seats sooner than expected.
issues.why: Owners report the leather finish fading, mostly from sun exposure.
issues.next: Use a sunshade and a leather conditioner. Ask the dealer whether it is covered under warranty.

issues.t: Dark patches in the headlight beam
issues.sym: At night you see dark spots or uneven patches in the light pattern on the road.
issues.why: An owner reports the dealer said Genesis knew of the uneven beam pattern but had no fix at the time.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the headlights and check for updated parts.

issues.t: Center screen or backup camera goes black
issues.sym: The main screen flickers, freezes or stays black, and the backup camera image may not appear in Reverse.
issues.why: Owners report the infotainment display and camera failing, sometimes coming back after a reboot. Dealers often can't find a code.
issues.next: Try a system restart, then have the dealer check for software updates and test the camera and wiring. Use your mirrors and look behind you until it is fixed.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes heavy or jerks, then the assist comes back after a few minutes.
issues.why: An owner reports the electric power steering losing assist while driving in the rain.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have the steering system and its codes checked by the dealer.

issues.t: Seat memory or easy-exit feature stops working
issues.sym: The driver seat no longer moves to its saved position, or the easy-exit feature doesn't move the seat back.
issues.why: An owner reports these seat features stopped working after a seat part was replaced.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to recheck the seat module and recalibrate the memory settings.

issues.t: Total electrical shutdown with doors locked
issues.sym: The car goes dead, the key fob, doors and trunk stop working, and it may need a tow. One owner reports being stuck inside for over 20 minutes.
issues.why: Owners report sudden loss of all power, sometimes with brake warnings. The exact cause has not been made public.
issues.next: Learn where the mechanical door release and hidden key are. Make sure all recalls are done and have the battery and electrical system checked.

issues.t: Brief delay in throttle response after stops
issues.sym: After stopping or turning, the car doesn't respond to the gas pedal for a second or two.
issues.why: An owner reports this happening many times. The dealer could not reproduce it, and a fuel pump recall covers some 2023 cars.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel pump recall is done, then ask the dealer to scan and road-test the car.

issues.t: Whining noise when slowing at highway speed
issues.sym: A loud whine from under the car when you lift off the gas at highway speed.
issues.why: An owner reports the noise when slowing from about 80 mph, similar to a known GV80 complaint.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the rear differential and driveline while the noise is happening.

issues.t: Wi-Fi, navigation or connected services stop working
issues.sym: Wi-Fi, calendar sync, navigation, weather or app features stop working for weeks at a time.
issues.why: An owner reports long-running software and connectivity faults that dealers have not fully fixed.
issues.next: Check for software updates and contact Genesis connected-services support. Keep records if it lasts.

issues.t: Driver attention alert goes off for no reason
issues.sym: The inattentive-driver warning beeps while you are watching the road, for example when wearing sunglasses.
issues.why: The driver monitoring camera can misread your eyes. An owner reports it can no longer be turned off on 2025 cars.
issues.next: Keep the camera lens clean. Ask the dealer about software updates.

issues.t: Tire pressure display missing from the dash
issues.sym: You can't find the tire pressure screen on the gauge display, and some menu options are missing.
issues.why: An owner reports the tire pressure menu and other options don't appear on the display.
issues.next: Check your tire pressures with a gauge. Ask the dealer about a software update.
